**Claim:** PM session `session_011SfZeFWrhGLHmfq61xbz4q` (`domain:ui` execution seat) — branch `claude/issue-6309-delete-object-fields-bridge`. `pm:queue` → `pm:dispatched` in the same label write.

## Pre-dispatch gate

**1. Thread read.** Triage comment (18:07:58Z) read in full. **Ruled: delete the module** plus the three prose references, per the **#6224 precedent** — zero importers with a working positive control, no planned consumer, and a header whose round-trip guarantee is measurably false for the designer-editable branch. ⛔ The keep-and-fix route was considered and rejected: it required a planned consumer and none exists.
**2. Shadow check.** Nothing in flight. Batch-mates: **#6396** (`components/renderers/form`) and **#6310** (`plugin-designer` + `i18n`). Checked against the batch as well as the in-flight set — no overlap with `app-shell/.../previews/`.
**3. Premise.** Measured by the filer on `origin/main @ 7ccb53a`. `main` has moved many times since — see below, this one is not optional.

## ⛔ Triage left a review-side instruction that lands on YOU first

> dead-code deletions get the reference-surface re-verified **on the merged base** — rerun the grep with its control before flipping anything.

**Re-run it, on current `main`, before you delete a line.** A dead-code deletion is only as good as the freshness of the reading that declared it dead, and the reading here is hours and many merges old. If a consumer has appeared since — **stop and report**; the ruling was conditional on there being none.

⭐ **And re-run the control, not just the search.** The filer's reading is trustworthy precisely because it carried one: the same command shape against the live sibling `object-fields-io` returns 10+ real consumers, proving the instrument finds consumers when they exist. A zero-hit grep with no control is not evidence of absence — it is equally consistent with a broken pattern. Report both numbers.

## Scope

Delete `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/object-fields-bridge.ts` (`bridgeFromDraft`, `commitToDraft`, `FieldsBridgeResult`) **and the three prose references** that still describe the bridge as wired — `types/src/designer.ts`, `types` `designer-field-types.test.ts` (×2), `fields` `richtext-cell-renderer-5452.test.tsx`.

⭐ Those comments are the reason this is a card and not a silent delete: they give a future reader three in-repo pointers claiming this bridge mediates something. Deleting the module and leaving the prose would swap dead code for **false documentation** — a worse outcome than either.

⛔ Do not touch `object-fields-io`, the live sibling. Do not "improve" anything else in `previews/`.

## Tests

- The check that matters is that **nothing breaks**: typecheck and the full affected-package suites must be green, and that is the evidence a zero-importer claim is true.
- ⛔ **The ghost-assertion guard does not apply in its usual form** — there is no new behaviour to pin, and inventing an assertion to satisfy the ritual would be theatre. Say so explicitly in the PR body rather than fabricating one. What replaces it: the **before/after reference-surface readings with their control**, quoted.
- If any test or typecheck references the deleted symbols, that is a consumer the grep missed — **stop and report**, do not adjust the test to make the deletion fit.

## Ground rules

Worktree-first: `git worktree add ../objectui-6309 -b claude/issue-6309-delete-object-fields-bridge main && cd ../objectui-6309 && pnpm install`. ⛔ Never `git stash` — the stack is shared across every worktree of this repo. ⛔ Never touch `content/docs/releases/`. Changeset: `patch`, per package changed. Open the PR as **draft** with `Fixes #6309` and report back — the PM lands it, ⛔ never self-merge.

Size: S. Model: opus.

## PM review — **ACCEPT**

PR #6414, head `21ea083b0`, cut from `062943f86`. `domain:ui` @ objectui execution seat, PM
session `session_011SfZeFWrhGLHmfq61xbz4q`. Re-verified against `origin/main` `64d888613`
independently of the report — a deletion is the one change class where the *absence* of evidence
is the whole argument, so the reference surface was re-measured rather than read.

### The reference surface, re-measured with its control

Outside the module itself, `object-fields-bridge` / `bridgeFromDraft` / `commitToDraft` /
`FieldsBridgeResult` occur **4 times across 3 files**, plus one changeset:

| site | kind |
|---|---|
| `packages/types/src/designer.ts:715` | prose comment |
| `packages/types/src/__tests__/designer-field-types.test.ts:14, :39` | prose comments |
| `packages/fields/src/__tests__/richtext-cell-renderer-5452.test.tsx:15` | prose comment |
| `.changeset/6043-retire-designer-formula-control.md:54` | past-tense record of another card |

**Zero `from` / `require` importing it. Zero call sites.** Confirmed.

⚠️ **One number in the report I could not reproduce, stated rather than smoothed over.** The
positive control (`object-fields-io`, same command shape) is reported as *109 hits / 29 files /
23 real imports*. My readings: **29 files repo-wide** — matching the report exactly — and 40 raw
hits; restricted to `packages/`, 24 files / 28 hits / 22 imports. So the *file* count reconciles
precisely at repo-wide scope and the import count is within one; only the raw-hit figure differs,
and that is the one number the control's argument does not rest on. The control does its job on
either reading: a live sibling with ~two dozen real importers, measured by the same command that
returns zero for the subject.

### What makes the zero-importer claim evidence rather than assertion

⭐ **Every test-file edit in the diff is inside a comment block.** I read the diff line by line:
every `+`/`-` line in `designer-field-types.test.ts` and `richtext-cell-renderer-5452.test.tsx`
begins with `*` or `//`. Not one assertion, import, or fixture moved. A deletion that required no
test to be adjusted is a deletion nothing depended on — that is the proof, and it is stronger
than the 7,697 passing tests quoted beside it.

### The prose repoint holds — and is better anchored than the report claims

Two comments naming the bridge as the consumer deriving an editable-subset check from
`DESIGNER_FIELD_TYPES` were repointed at `MetadataFieldsPage`. Verified live:

```
packages/plugin-designer/src/MetadataFieldsPage.tsx:34  import { DESIGNER_FIELD_TYPES } from '@object-ui/types';
packages/plugin-designer/src/MetadataFieldsPage.tsx:96  // Derived from the canonical vocabulary rather than restated (objectui#3017).
packages/plugin-designer/src/MetadataFieldsPage.tsx:97  const KNOWN_FIELD_TYPES: ReadonlySet<DesignerFieldType> = new Set(DESIGNER_FIELD_TYPES);
```

Same idiom, and the substitute carries the **same `objectui#3017` anchor in its own comment** —
so the repointed prose is not merely plausible, it is true of a site that already documents itself
the same way. Exported at `index.tsx:79`, referenced by 6 test files.

⭐ **And the two clauses with no live referent were dropped, not repointed.** The bridge
round-trip re-check instruction and the richtext→html mapping as third corroboration both went,
rather than being aimed at an unverified stand-in. That is the harder and the right call:
repointing prose at a substitute you have not confirmed is how a comment becomes false silently.
The richtext test's header now stands on two sources instead of three, which is honest about what
survives.

The surviving mention in `.changeset/6043-…md` was correctly left alone — it is a past-tense
record of what #6043 did, not a claim the bridge is wired, and editing another card's changeset
would be out of scope.

### Beyond the grep

`@object-ui/app-shell`'s exports map declares only `.` and `./styles.css`, so the module was never
reachable as a deep import — that closes the one hole a source-tree grep leaves open, and it was
checked rather than assumed.

### Landing

CI at `21ea083b0`: 24 checks complete and green, 4 test shards still running, **0 failures**.
⛔ Not enqueued yet — 入队资格 is *every* check green, not the required subset. It goes to the
merge queue when the shards land.
